claims.text: Catalytic activity and selectivity of supported transition-metal catalysts are primarily governed by the degree of metal-support electronic interaction.
Enhanced electron donation at the metal-support interface shifts the d-band center of active sites.
Electronic-structure modulation strengthens or otherwise favors adsorption of key reaction intermediates.
More favorable adsorption of key intermediates accelerates catalytic conversion.
PtPdCoCuNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles can be prepared on SiO2 with uniform nanoparticle dispersion.
Controlled support doping or interface modification can systematically enhance metal-support electronic interactions relative to an unmodified baseline.
Electronic effects dominate nitrobenzene hydrogenation around 80 °C under suitable controlled pressures and feed compositions.
Metal-support interactions modulate the interfacial d-band center and charge distribution at metal sites.
Electron donation increases electron density at noble-metal sites such as Pt and Pd.
Charge transfer to Pt and Pd sites modulates nitrobenzene adsorption.
Electronic gradients in a high-entropy alloy modulate hydrogen-intermediate adsorption in HER.
Selectivity improves because enhanced metal-support electron donation suppresses side reactions.
Engineered supports with enhanced metal-support interactions will produce higher activity than unmodified supports.
Engineered supports will produce XPS or DRIFTS shifts consistent with a modified electronic environment.
The proposed relationship holds when electronic effects dominate over mass transport and thermal sintering.
Isolated Pt and Pd sites and charge transfer from less expensive transition metals to those noble-metal sites are associated with enhanced nitrobenzene adsorption and hydrogenation activity.
An unstrained HEA surface can outperform Pt(111), potentially because heterogeneous electronic gradients alter hydrogen adsorption energies.
Geometric effects and particle-size changes may also contribute to the observed catalytic behavior.
